clue.text: Bail imposed here after vote?

definitions.meaning: in cricket the bails rest on top of the stumps, so a bail sits there
a politician touring to seek votes is out campaigning, after the vote in the sense of chasing it

explanation.walkthrough: Cricket's bails are the two small crosspieces balanced on top of the three stumps; 'after' means pursuing, not following in time.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers both the bail's resting place atop the wicket and a politician out campaigning for support.

clue.text: Unlimited dictionary containing something for writer to chew on?

indicators.note: containing means the dictionary letters go around the rest

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

parts.words: something for writer to chew on
parts.note: a writer thinking hard chews the end of a pen

explanation.surface: Asks whether a dictionary holds endless food for thought for writers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open-ended has no fixed limit or conclusion.

clue.text: Switched to light, round goods

indicators.note: round means the first words go around the goods

parts.note: led is a past tense of light, as in led the way, or a light-emitting diode
G stands for good, doubled here for the plural

explanation.surface: Someone flicked to the light setting, surrounded by merchandise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' is not lit here: LED is the light-emitting diode. 'round' is the container signal, not a circle giving O.
explanation.definitionFit: To toggle is to switch between two states, so toggled means switched.

clue.text: Plant making paste?

parts.note: paste is imitation gemstone, so a fake stone, and the plant's name splits as a fake plus a stone

explanation.definitionFit: The three-leaved clover that is Ireland's emblem is a plant whose name breaks into fake plus stone.

clue.text: Sprinkles amount unevenly, being unfair

indicators.note: sprinkled unevenly suggests the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who shares out sprinkles in uneven amounts is being unfair.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsportsmanlike conduct breaks the spirit of fair play.

clue.text: Stars fail to turn up on farm

definitions.meaning: the seven bright stars of Ursa Major are called this in Britain, the Big Dipper elsewhere
in old British university slang, to fail an exam candidate
to break up and turn over soil in a field

explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: the British name for the Big Dipper, old slang for failing an exam, and the farming verb.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers the star group, the examiners' slang for failing, and turning soil on a farm.

clue.text: Middle class American colonist

definitions.meaning: an acronym for a White Anglo-Saxon Protestant, the stereotypical comfortable establishment American
the insect lives in a social colony with a queen and workers

explanation.definitionFit: The acronym names a stereotyped establishment American, and the stinging insect is a colony-dweller.

clue.text: Monday evening? Just a minute sir!

parts.note: minute, meaning tiny, is wee in Scots
Sir is the title of a knight

explanation.surface: Someone calls out to a gentleman on a Monday night asking him to wait a minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just a minute' looks like a request to wait; 'minute' is the adjective meaning tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Monday evening is an example of a weeknight, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Having means to complete crossword books

parts.note: to complete a crossword is to solve it
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: Being able to finish the crossword books shows means.
explanation.definitionFit: Solvent means able to pay one's debts, having enough money.

clue.text: With advantage, means to bring side on

parts.note: an edge is a slight advantage over a rival
ways are means or methods of doing something

explanation.surface: Someone explains how an advantage can be used to bring a flank into play.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving something edgeways means presenting its narrow side first, i.e. side on.

clue.text: None divulge love for opera

parts.note: O, the figure zero, stands for none
to divulge a secret is to tell it
love is zero in tennis scoring, hence O

explanation.surface: Nobody will reveal their affection for the opera house.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's late opera on Shakespeare's Moor of Venice carries this Italian title.

clue.text: Miss point entirely when reflecting

parts.note: E, east, is one of the compass points

indicators.note: reflecting, as in a mirror, means the word just before is turned round

parts.note: entirely means all, wholly

explanation.surface: Someone misses the point completely while lost in thought.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's first name, so a young woman who might be addressed as Miss.

clue.text: Spice got in foreign parts I understand

indicators.note: parts means separates, so the radio word is split open to take the jumbled letters

parts.note: Roger is radio language for message received and understood

indicators.note: foreign suggests the letters of the two words are made strange, rearranged

explanation.surface: A traveller acquired spices abroad and claims to know about them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I understand' is radio procedure: Roger confirms a message received. 'foreign' scrambles the two words, and 'parts' opens up the radio word to take them.
explanation.definitionFit: The dried rhizome of the ginger plant is a familiar kitchen spice.

clue.text: Part of Kansas ultimately recalled in description of old Venice

indicators.note: this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round

parts.note: old Venice was ruled by a doge, so it could be described as a doge city

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word recalled

explanation.surface: A remembered piece of Kansas sits oddly inside an account of historic Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: The Doge was the elected ruler of the old Venetian republic.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wild West cattle town is a city in the state of Kansas.

clue.text: Raised gallery in upper wall is easily reached

indicators.note: in means the reversed gallery sits inside the wall

parts.note: a gable is the triangular upper part of an end wall

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is read upwards, reversed

parts.note: the Tate is a famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: A raised gallery high on a wall can be reached easily.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'Raised' reads the gallery upwards; 'in' puts that inside the wall's upper part. The Tate is London's best-known art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Something get-at-able is accessible, easy to get hold of.

clue.text: A paying audience for rock with bands

parts.note: the gate is the paying crowd at a sports match, or the money taken

explanation.surface: A paying crowd turns out for a rock concert featuring several groups.
explanation.definitionFit: This semi-precious stone is a form of chalcedony famous for its coloured stripes.

clue.text: Irritation that's right inside diseased retina?

indicators.note: inside means the agreement goes within the jumbled letters
diseased suggests the word retina is disordered, its letters rearranged

parts.note: yes is said to agree that something is right

explanation.surface: Asks whether eye irritation comes from something lodged in an unhealthy retina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diseased' scrambles the eye part's letters and 'inside' tucks the agreement among them; the question mark admits the surface is only nearly a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyestrain is a tired, sore feeling in the eyes, a kind of irritation.

clue.text: It surfaces, threatening to pounce at the outset

parts.note: black clouds or looks are threatening

indicators.note: at the outset means the start of the word pounce

explanation.surface: Something emerges, menacing and ready to spring from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It surfaces' suggests a creature coming up; it is a material that surfaces roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Blacktop is asphalt used to surface roads and paths, so it is what surfaces them.

clue.text: Barking like a Dalmatian?

definitions.meaning: barking, short for barking mad, means crazy
the dog's coat is covered in spots, so it is spotty or covered in dots

explanation.definitionFit: The word means slightly crazy, and literally describes something covered in spots like a Dalmatian.

clue.text: All the family at home in Scotland presumably causes battle!

parts.words: All the family at home in Scotland presumably
parts.note: if the whole family is at home then none of the relatives is away, said in Scots with its clipped word for away

explanation.surface: A Scottish family gathering at home turns into a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The Second World War battle for the Japanese island is named; 'presumably' flags the jokey Scots spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1945 Pacific campaign on this Japanese island was one of the bloodiest battles of the war.

clue.text: Petty officer and lieutenant hiding in a tree

parts.note: SM, sergeant major, is a senior non-commissioned officer

indicators.note: hiding in means the officer's abbreviation is concealed within the tree

parts.note: the lime or linden is a tree

explanation.surface: A petty officer and a lieutenant are hiding up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Petty officer' reads as a naval rank, but 'Petty' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Small-time means minor or unimportant, the same sense as petty.

clue.text: Rob and I at sea on ship

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Two people are at sea together aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Inboard means inside the hull of a ship, i.e. on ship.

clue.text: Edith when eating left with fine rice dish

indicators.note: eating means the singer's name takes the next letter inside

parts.note: Edith Piaf was the French singer
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Edith eats a fine rice dish with her left hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilaff is a dish of rice cooked in stock with spices.

clue.text: Theatrical fellow's order to hold right back

indicators.note: to hold means the first pieces contain the next one inside them

parts.note: his, belonging to a fellow
Ionic is one of the classical orders of architecture

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation is read in reverse

explanation.surface: An actor orders someone to keep the right side back on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' is architectural, not a command: the Ionic order of columns. 'back' turns the abbreviation and 'to hold' wraps the other pieces round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Histrionic behaviour is exaggerated and stagey, so theatrical in the figurative sense.

clue.text: Egg on toast, eggs Benedict, apple turnover for starters

indicators.note: turnover means the gathered letters are flipped end to end
starters are the opening letters of each of the four food words

explanation.surface: A brunch menu: egg on toast, eggs Benedict and an apple turnover to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters give TEBA, and 'turnover' reverses them. 'Egg on' looks like part of the menu but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet someone is to encourage or urge them on, the same as to egg them on.

clue.text: Letter from Greek essayist and lawyer

parts.note: Charles Lamb was the English essayist who wrote as Elia
DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer

explanation.surface: A letter arrives from a Greek writer of essays who is also a lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: The eleventh letter of the Greek alphabet, corresponding to our L.

clue.text: Rising, had a fit, niftily turning back covers

indicators.note: turning back means the concealed letters are read from right to left
covers means the words conceal the answer within their letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone stood up, threw a tantrum, and deftly turned back the bedclothes.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'turning back covers' as the definition; it is the two indicators, and 'Rising' (an uprising) is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arabic term names a Palestinian uprising against occupation, so a rising.

clue.text: Throw from stage to audience

indicators.note: to an audience means as heard by listeners, a sound-alike

parts.note: a phase is a stage in a process

explanation.surface: An actor throws something from the stage into the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw someone, in the sense of disconcerting them, is to faze them.

clue.text: What follows King intervening in charge?

definitions.text: What follows King intervening in charge?

indicators.note: follows means the word before is placed after the first part
intervening in means the King's letter comes between the letters of the charge

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service
R, from Rex, is the abbreviation for King
Pardon? is a polite way of saying What? when you mishear

explanation.surface: A question about what happens when the monarch steps into a criminal case.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole, the clue describes what results when the sovereign intervenes in a criminal charge: a royal pardon.
explanation.definitionFit: A full pardon granted by the Crown wipes out a conviction, the outcome of royal intervention in a charge.
